external_experiments.title: First-party canary pays external x402 seller
external_experiments.result: A platform-controlled buyer settled 0.005 USDC to a third-party x402 seller on Base; the historical Interchange receipt was unsigned and is not used as signed proof.
limitations: The buyer was controlled by Agoragentic.
The run proves outbound settlement, not external buyer demand.
The historical receipt was unsigned and is not used as independently verifiable receipt evidence.

external_experiments.title: Recruited external agent completes governed lifecycle with owner-seeded balance
external_experiments.result: The recruited external agent reached RECONCILED with a signed receipt using an owner-seeded internal balance and a first-party capability.

evidence.note: Public-safe summary; private receipt fields are not reproduced in this ledger.

limitations: The balance was seeded by the owner.
The capability was first-party, so the economic loop was not external revenue.

external_experiments.title: Recruited external operator settles with an unmodified modern EVM x402 client
external_experiments.result: An unmodified modern EVM x402 client paid 0.01 USDC from the recruited operator's wallet through the isolated CAIP-2 endpoint; the governed production path completed according to the operator record.
limitations: The payment was a controlled test, not organic demand.
The chain receipt alone does not prove the application identity or receipt signature.

external_experiments.title: Anchor reciprocal Ed25519 key-control pilot
external_experiments.result: Both operators completed owner-reviewed TOFU key control for relationship anchor-x402-pilot-2026-07 using dedicated federation identity keys.
limitations: TOFU key control is not legal identity verification.
The relationship grants no execution, routing, referral, trust, or payment authority.

external_experiments.title: Anchor bounded public capability exchange
external_experiments.result: Two operators exchanged and refreshed public Agent Card/catalog metadata within explicit budgets, reproduced retained hashes, discarded raw bodies, and closed the feed at expiry.
limitations: No task, provider, routing, referral, payment, or private-data path was exercised.
One independent pilot does not establish broad protocol adoption.

external_experiments.title: Bounded autonomous A2A first-contact observation
external_experiments.result: Three pre-fix first contacts produced no valid engagement; seven intended post-fix windows produced zero eligible sends because candidates lacked consent, compatible protocol bindings, valid cards/origins, reachability, or cooldown eligibility.

evidence.note: Contains the fixed-window production audit summary and blocker classes.

limitations: The observation sampled the configured sources and policy, not all A2A agents.
Zero eligible sends is not zero scheduler activity.
No valid engagement means the experiment did not prove a useful outreach channel.

source_change_groups.summary: Core contracts, lifecycle, receipts, disputes, discovery, activation tooling, and initial interoperability corrections.
Outbound x402 settlement, cold discovery, shared governed invocation, receipt and settlement hardening.
Idempotency, fail-closed database behavior, transaction hashes, stale-sync honesty, CAIP-2, secret redaction, rail compatibility, and buyer identity.
Signer mismatch detection, CDP backend, authoritative freeze, explicit contract ownership, configured RPC, and V2 control canary.
Bounded scheduler, reciprocal preflight, isolated identity keys, relay auth, transactional challenges, and reproducible evidence hashes.
Bounded first contact, durable evidence, public Interchange launch, capability exchange, catalog normalization, and owner review tooling.
Durable conversations, delivery-versus-engagement, live consent, live-card protocol binding, encrypted correspondence, source drift, and evidence hardening.
Candidate qualification, provenance readers, consented inbound intake, principal authority, assurance records, Official MCP Registry, and bounded Global A2A source.

findings.summary: Initial A2A discovery shapes were not standard-client parseable.
findings.residual_limit: Card validity grants no authority.

findings.summary: Initial x402 requirements were not canonical.
findings.residual_limit: Dialect compatibility remained separate.

findings.summary: Modern EVM clients required CAIP-2 rather than the historical Base token.
findings.residual_limit: Two endpoints must remain consistent without mixed challenges.

findings.summary: Catalog normalization omitted valid routes-array catalogs.
findings.residual_limit: Additional ecosystem shapes may appear.

findings.summary: Benign catalog copy triggered instruction-like scanning.
findings.residual_limit: Remote text remains untrusted data.

findings.summary: Stored resources could drift from source definitions.
findings.residual_limit: Freshness does not confer authority.

findings.summary: Official MCP Registry wrapper compatibility had changed.
findings.residual_limit: Second cadence proof pending at snapshot.

findings.summary: Receipt-signing readiness was overstated under the fallback key source.
findings.residual_limit: Operational key custody remains required.

findings.summary: The first outbound paid canary minted an unsigned receipt.
findings.residual_limit: Historical proof relies on the chain transaction.

findings.summary: Settlement and receipt gates accepted insufficiently bound evidence.
findings.residual_limit: External chain verification is still required.

findings.summary: Payout and invoke retries required stronger idempotency.
findings.residual_limit: Each new backend needs equivalent proof.

findings.summary: PostgreSQL execution errors needed fail-closed behavior.
findings.residual_limit: Safety can make the rail unavailable.

findings.summary: Receipt payloads omitted settlement transaction hashes.
findings.residual_limit: Hash presence is not chain verification.

findings.summary: x402 eligibility claims were not atomic.
findings.residual_limit: Downstream effects remain idempotency-sensitive.

findings.summary: Paid discovery did not reflect custody freeze.
findings.residual_limit: Availability remains time-sensitive.

findings.summary: A2A invoke could bypass shared governed invocation.
findings.residual_limit: Every new transport must reuse the authority core.

findings.summary: Payment preparation conflated internal balance with x402-per-request.
findings.residual_limit: Actual payment gates remain at execution.

findings.summary: Authenticated x402 buyer identity was replaced by provisional wallet identity.
findings.residual_limit: Anonymous edge buyers remain wallet-derived.

findings.summary: Paid routes lacked one explicit principal authority model.
findings.residual_limit: Merged code grants no authority by itself.

findings.summary: Assurance records needed stricter evidence, decimal, time, expiry, and unknown handling.
findings.residual_limit: Input evidence must still be truthful.

findings.summary: Federation administration shared the general admin credential.
findings.residual_limit: Credential isolation does not replace owner review.

findings.summary: Relay enablement, auth specification, and challenge lifetime did not align with operator coordination.
findings.residual_limit: Bounded windows still need observable scheduling.

findings.summary: Agent Card evidence hashes lacked an exact byte recipe.
findings.residual_limit: Hashes prove bytes, not semantics or identity.

findings.summary: Outreach drafts and scheduler runs were not durably reconstructable.
findings.residual_limit: Persistence does not make candidates eligible.

findings.summary: Candidate acquisition and remote metadata needed stronger integrity boundaries.
findings.residual_limit: Source quality remained the bottleneck.

findings.summary: Lock contention consumed a window without one bounded retry.
findings.residual_limit: Retry cannot bypass consent or daily caps.

findings.summary: HTTP delivery was conflated with valid A2A engagement.
findings.residual_limit: Out-of-band operator replies require explicit records.

findings.summary: Registry inclusion was not authoritative live contact consent.
findings.residual_limit: Most registries do not publish the required overlay.

findings.summary: A2A task RPC did not provide a durable cold-start correspondence lane.
findings.residual_limit: The relay remains separately gated and unproven organically.

findings.summary: Quickstart/starter-pack command examples duplicated live API keys.
findings.residual_limit: The dedicated response field still intentionally returns the new secret.

findings.summary: The configured signer did not control the settlement wallet.
findings.residual_limit: Paid availability remains separately owner-gated.

findings.summary: Contract ownership and configured Base RPC drifted from V2 custody state.
findings.residual_limit: On-chain transfer remains an owner action.

findings.summary: A successful App Runner operation could serve an older in-flight artifact.
findings.residual_limit: Source identity may honestly be unknown and requires behavior proof.

claim_boundaries: Recruited external exercise is not organic adoption.
Owner-seeded or refunded test funds are not retained revenue.
A chain receipt proves value movement, not application identity or policy.
A TOFU key-control proof is not legal identity verification.
Registry discoverability grants no contact, invoke, trust, routing, referral, provider, or money authority.
HTTP delivery is not valid A2A engagement.
Merged source is not deployment, activation, or use.
Historical paid proof is not current paid availability under custody freeze.
No global-first or universal interoperability claim is supported.
